activities.caption: one line of the cheat-sheet hides a tragedy
activities.name: nbGroupsSpot

config.prompt: A functional-group cheat-sheet — one line is wrong. Click it:
lines: Carboxyl (−COOH): an acid end — pairs with alcohols to form esters.
Amine (−NH₂): a basic end — pairs with acids to form amides, the protein link.
Chirality is a cosmetic curiosity: mirror-image forms behave identically in the body.
Every implant's surface chemistry traces back to which groups are on display.
config.correction: Mirror-image (chiral) forms are different substances biologically — the body's receptors are chiral. One mirror form of thalidomide was a sedative while the other, interconverting in the body, was a teratogen.
config.why: The same atoms in different arrangements are different substances: isomerism is design information, not a footnote.

activities.anchor: Same monomer, different chain length, different world
activities.caption: drag between the two chain-building families
activities.name: nbChainCompare

config.prompt: Two great families of chain-building — drag between their growth logic:

before.label: addition (chain-growth)
before.text: A double bond is opened by an initiator; the radical zips monomers down one chain to completion in microseconds. Needs the C=C — ethylene into polyethylene.

after.label: condensation (step-growth)
after.text: Bifunctional monomers join pairwise, losing a small molecule (water) each time; every chain end reacts with every other, and useful molecular mass waits for very high conversion — Carothers' rule.

config.why: Chains either way — but the growth logic is opposite, and condensation is the same mechanism biology runs on to build protein.

activities.anchor: Crosslink density is the fine dial
activities.caption: set the glass transition that splits fridge liner from cup
activities.name: nbTgPlace

config.prompt: Polypropylene's side groups are small, polystyrene's are bulky. Place polypropylene's glass transition temperature:
config.why: Near −10 °C: flexible at room temperature (fridge liners). Polystyrene sits near +100 °C — brittle glass at room temperature, the disposable cup. One structural detail, a 110-degree shift.

activities.caption: file each plastic by what the melt allows
activities.name: nbRecycleBuckets

config.prompt: "Plastic is one meltable substance" — file each case:

items.label: one stray PVC bottle in a PET batch

config.why: Thermosets and crosslinked elastomers never melt again; mixed thermoplastics separate like oil and water — which is why recycling sorts by resin code. Polymer identity is architecture.

activities.caption: call the wavelength that turns gold ruby-red
activities.name: nbPlasmonEstimate

config.prompt: Gold nanoparticles 10–20 nm across look ruby-red because their conduction electrons resonate with light. Roughly what wavelength (nm) is the surface plasmon resonance?
config.why: Near 520 nm — green light absorbed, red reflected: the same physics that made medieval ruby glass. Bigger dot, redder emission for quantum dots — colour as a geometric parameter.
config.context: Composition plus architecture: two knobs where bulk materials had one, and the second is free at the nanoscale.

config.prompt: One element, three forms — drag the family chronicle into order:
items: 1985 — fullerene: 60 atoms curled into a closed ball, found by mass spectrometry of laser-vaporised graphite
1991 — Iijima's carbon nanotube: the same honeycomb sheet rolled into a cylinder of ~100 GPa tensile strength
roll angle tunes the tube — carrying current like a metal or semiconducting
2004 — graphene: one atomic layer peeled with adhesive tape; the 2010 Nobel for Geim and Novoselov
the 2-D zoo follows — MoS₂, hBN, phosphorene — out of the tape dispenser
config.why: Carbon's sp² bonding built the whole family — and a first-year lab technique opened the continent that precision equipment had been unknowingly producing for 150 years.

activities.caption: pair each biological architecture with its principle
activities.name: nbBioMatch

config.prompt: Nature's prior art — pair each architecture with the design principle it teaches:

pairs.right: platelets slide, crack paths zigzag: ~3,000 times tougher than the mineral alone

pairs.left: bone — hydroxyapatite platelets inside collagen fibrils
gecko feet — billions of nanoscale spatulae
pairs.right: van der Waals forces summed over astronomical contact area

pairs.left: lotus leaf — micron bumps under nanoscale wax crystals
pairs.right: water balls and self-cleans — the lotus effect, now in paint and fabric

config.why: Biology achieves property X with abundant materials at ambient temperature, by architecture alone — and the 4-billion-year database is open.

activities.anchor: condensation chemistry as a dosage form
activities.caption: walk the implant-material decision
activities.name: nbImplantBranch

config.root: The design environment: 37 °C, salty, oxygen-rich, immune-active. Choose the material for the job.

start.text: The device must bond directly to living bone. Which specification do you write?

choices.label: Titanium — and let its oxide surface do the work
choices.feedback: The orthopaedic standard, for a reason the metal alone does not explain.

choices.label: Cobalt-chrome throughout
choices.feedback: A superb load-bearer — but bearing load is not this job's whole spec.

ti.text: Osseointegration: bone grows into direct structural contact with the oxide surface — Brånemark's discovery in the 1950s–60s, now the basis of millions of dental and hip implants. The right interaction beats mere inertness.

cc.text: Cobalt-chrome carries joint loads superbly, but nothing in it invites bone into structural contact. For osseointegration, titanium's oxide wins — cobalt-chrome keeps the jobs where load-bearing is the whole story.

degra.text: A scaffold that must vanish as tissue regrows: poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) hydrolyses on a tunable schedule — weeks to months, set by the lactide:glycolide ratio. The implant whose success is its own disappearance.

config.why: Biocompatibility is not inertness but the right interaction — and controlled degradation makes the implant's disappearance its success metric.
